items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: He was with Simon Stewart later.

ctx.x: at Harman's, Elvis Band at Harman's Dreamland. Well, I somehow get Sudler and another good trumpet player, a man from Louisville in the entertainers at some period. And I don't know who, what band it would be with. Bobby somebody, two trumpet players, and they work well as a team, Sudler and... Oh, let's see. Several people... After we left... They never recorded, Sudler never played a hot chorus on record, so we don't know. No,

no. He really was a tough man. He had a tough lip and he could hit the high notes. He really could play. He was with Simon Stewart later. Yeah, he was with Simon Stewart later. And after we left the entertainers' cafe, we went to Joe Garman's Paradise there at Prairie and 35th. And that's when I wrote that 35th Street thing that they call the blues. Which isn't the blues. Oh, that's the 35th... It just says 35th Street, and I gave it to Mayo Williams. He was with Paramount Records. Mayo liked it, and he said, I'm…
